classification.difficultyReason: Use exact reference angles and quadrant signs, then generate and filter coterminal solutions across different domains containing negative angles. The widest domain requires four tangent solutions; the secant part also requires reciprocal conversion.

content.prompt: Solve the following equations in the provided domain.

answer.worked:
The related acute angle is $60^\circ$. Within the given domain, sine is positive only for angles in quadrants I and II.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=60^\circ,\ 180^\circ-60^\circ\\\theta&=60^\circ,120^\circ\end{align*}$$

The related acute angle is $45^\circ$. Cosine is negative at the second- and third-quadrant angles; express both within the given domain.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=-180^\circ+45^\circ,\ 180^\circ-45^\circ\\\theta&=-135^\circ,135^\circ\end{align*}$$

The related acute angle is $60^\circ$. Tangent is negative in quadrants II and IV, giving $120^\circ$ and $300^\circ$ in one positive revolution. Subtract $360^\circ$ to obtain the negative solutions in the domain.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=120^\circ-360^\circ,\ 300^\circ-360^\circ,\ 120^\circ,300^\circ\\\theta&=-240^\circ,-60^\circ,120^\circ,300^\circ\end{align*}$$

$$\cos\theta=\frac12$$
The related acute angle is $60^\circ$. The cosine solutions are $60^\circ$ and $300^\circ$ in one positive revolution. Since $300^\circ$ lies outside the domain, use its coterminal angle $300^\circ-360^\circ=-60^\circ$. Thus $\theta=-60^\circ,60^\circ$.
